config.title: Hiring & interviews

intro.title: Hiring & interviews
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a structured interview evaluation system to practice fair and effective hiring principles. You will learn how to define clear evaluation criteria, create a scoring mechanism, and implement a decision-making process based on candidate scores. The core concepts involve using structured data, conditional logic, and systematic workflows to simulate a real-world interview review. This exercise will help you understand how to standardize interviews to reduce bias and make data-driven hiring decisions.
intro.usecase: Hiring and interview systems are critical components of modern HR platforms like Greenhouse, Lever, and Workday. Developers build candidate dashboards that display applicant pipelines, interview scheduling interfaces that coordinate multiple calendars, and structured evaluation forms that standardize feedback across hiring teams. These systems require careful state management for candidate status, interview workflows, and collaborative scoring mechanisms that multiple stakeholders access simultaneously. Implementing robust hiring interfaces directly impacts an organization's ability to scale talent acquisition efficiently while maintaining consistent evaluation standards.

objectives: Construct a structured interview process with defined stages and evaluation criteria
Implement a candidate scoring system that aggregates feedback from multiple interviewers
Configure a hiring pipeline dashboard to visualize candidate progress and status
Apply behavioral interview frameworks to design standardized question sets
Integrate diverse feedback sources to create comprehensive candidate profiles
Manipulate hiring metrics to identify bottlenecks and optimize the recruitment workflow
Initialize a structured debrief process that synthesizes interview data into hiring decisions

steps.analogousExample:

import React, { useState } from 'react';

steps.title: Create the HiringDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named HiringDashboard that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax, and make sure it returns a div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the HiringDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A HiringDashboard component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named HiringDashboard and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly HiringDashboard and returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize candidate data state
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, use useState to create a state variable named 'candidates' initialized with an array of candidate objects. Each object should have id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.
steps.hint: Initialize useState with an array containing at least one candidate object. Example: { id: 1, name: 'Alex Chen', role: 'Frontend Engineer', interviewStage: 'Technical' }
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a candidates state variable containing an array of candidate objects with the required properties.
successCriteria: candidates state is declared with useState, initialized with an array of objects, and each object has id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with state initialization. Make sure your candidates array contains at least one complete candidate object with all four required properties: id, name, role, and interviewStage.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing the candidates state. Use useState to create a state variable named 'candidates' initialized with an array of objects containing id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.

steps.title: Define filter handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, create a function named handleFilterChange that takes a newFilter parameter and updates the roleFilter state with it.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setRoleFilter with the provided newFilter value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleFilterChange function is defined that updates the roleFilter state when called with a new filter value.
successCriteria: The component contains a handleFilterChange function that accepts a parameter and calls setRoleFilter with it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts a parameter and calls setRoleFilter with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named handleFilterChange that takes a parameter and updates the roleFilter state.

steps.title: Define stage update handler
steps.instruction: Inside your HiringDashboard component, create a function named handleStageUpdate that takes candidateId and newStage as parameters and updates the candidate's interviewStage in the candidates state.
steps.hint: You'll need to use setCandidates to update the state. Map through the candidates array and update the matching candidate's interviewStage.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleStageUpdate function is defined that properly updates a candidate's interview stage when provided with their ID and the new stage.
successCriteria: The handleStageUpdate function is defined with candidateId and newStage parameters, uses setCandidates to update state, and correctly maps through candidates to update the matching candidate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly updates the candidates state using setCandidates and the map method to find and update the correct candidate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create handleStageUpdate with two parameters and use setCandidates to update the state by mapping through candidates.

steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a <section> element with a heading 'Filter Candidates' and a <select> dropdown for role filtering. The select should have an onChange event wired to handleFilterChange and its value bound to roleFilter state.
steps.hint: Add the section after the return statement. Include a <label> for the select with appropriate text.

steps.title: Add stage progression buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the candidates display section, for each candidate, add buttons to move between interview stages: 'Phone Screen', 'Technical', 'Behavioral', and 'Offer'. Wire each button's onClick event to call handleStageUpdate with the candidate's id and the target stage.
steps.hint: Map over the candidates array and render buttons for each stage. Pass the candidate id and the target stage string to handleStageUpdate when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each candidate in the display section will have four buttons representing interview stages, allowing users to simulate moving candidates through the hiring pipeline.
successCriteria: Buttons for 'Phone Screen', 'Technical', 'Behavioral', and 'Offer' are rendered for each candidate with onClick handlers that call handleStageUpdate with the candidate id and target stage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure all four stage buttons are present for each candidate and properly wired to handleStageUpdate with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stage progression buttons are missing or not properly configured. Each candidate needs four buttons with onClick handlers that call handleStageUpdate with the candidate id and target stage.
